# Break-glass + backups

<!-- Generated by `go run docs/roadmap/gen.go docs` from tickets.json. Do not edit by hand. -->

**Phase:** [P1 · Who did it](../README.md#phase-1--who-did-it) · **Lane:** Control plane · **Label:** `feature:ops-hardening` · **Epic:** [#55](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/55) · **Tickets:** 11 (8S 3M)

Operators get a local emergency admin login for when Dex is down. It is off by default, needs TLS, uses an argon2id hash, and every attempt writes an audit row, an ERROR log line and an alert. The CP also takes scheduled, consistent backups of its SQLite state and served config under a state-dir lock, ships a restore command that refuses unsafe restores, and documents the restore drill and a production readiness checklist.

## How we build it

- Scope and back-compat: break-glass and backups are both off by default. Both need --state-dir (cpstate). Break-glass also needs console.auth=oidc; validation rejects it with auth none. Workers are unchanged and nothing runs on the request hot path. When p5-postgres-ha replaces SQLite, the backup job is disabled in Postgres mode.
- Degraded mode: break-glass only helps if the CP starts and serves while Dex is down. With the issuer unreachable the CP must still serve /policy, /control/heartbeat and /central/ingest, and /auth/login returns 503 idp_unavailable while discovery retries with backoff. This is a requirement on W-P1-SSO-03 (lazy discovery). It is tested in-process in W-P1-OPS1-09 (TestControlPlaneBreakGlassDegraded, issuer unreachable) and against the real Dex container in W-P1-OPS1-10 (L2, Dex stopped and the CP restarted).
- Config (W-P1-OPS1-01 adds the field, its parsing and validation to the W-P1-SSO-02 ConsoleConfig): `console.breakGlass: {enabled: false, username, passwordHashEnv | passwordHashFile, sessionTTL: 1h (max 4h), allowBehindTLSTerminator: false}`. The hash is an argon2id PHC string (new dependencies golang.org/x/crypto/argon2 and golang.org/x/term, each with an architecture.yaml S3 manifest entry; PHC encode/parse is written in Warden). Parameters are bounded: m 19456..262144 KiB, t 2..10, p 1..4, salt >= 16 bytes, key >= 32 bytes. passwordHashFile is re-read on each attempt so a mounted secret can rotate without a CP restart. The block is CP-local and never rides policyWire. W-P1-OPS1-09 checks at startup that --state-dir is set and that the hash parses.
- TLS: startup fails when break-glass is enabled and the CP serves plain HTTP on a non-loopback --listen address, unless allowBehindTLSTerminator is true. In that case the session cookie is still marked Secure.
- `warden control-plane hash-password` reads the password from a TTY with echo off (confirmed twice) or from stdin with --stdin, never from argv. It rejects passwords shorter than 16 characters and prints only the PHC string (m=65536 KiB, t=3, p=2).
- Login (W-P1-OPS1-08): `POST /auth/breakglass` is mounted only when enabled and returns 404 otherwise. It is a public pre-auth route in the W-P1-SSO-05 authz table, exempt from the W-P1-SSO-04 CSRF check and from the W-P1-AAUD-02 audit middleware (the handler writes its own row). It requires Content-Type application/json, a same-origin Origin header when one is sent, and a body of at most 4 KiB. Order: rate limit, then a 2-slot verify semaphore (429 when full), then argon2id verify. Verify always runs, against a fixed dummy hash when the username does not match, and the username is compared with subtle.ConstantTimeCompare, so wrong user and wrong password take the same time and return the same 401 body.
- Rate limits: 5 failed attempts per 15 min per r.RemoteAddr host (X-Forwarded-For is not trusted), plus a global ceiling of 20 failed attempts per 15 min, so one attacker behind a shared load balancer address is still bounded. The limiter is in memory and resets on CP restart; this is documented.
- Session (W-P1-OPS1-08, W-P1-OPS1-09): success revokes any earlier break-glass session and creates a session with role admin, auth_method `breakglass`, sub `breakglass:<configured username>`, an absolute expiry of sessionTTL and no idle extension. /auth/me (W-P1-SSO-04) already returns authMethod and expiresAt, and the dashboard shows a red banner with the expiry time. While a break-glass session is active the CP logs a WARN every 5 minutes.
- Loud on every attempt (W-P1-OPS1-08): the handler writes exactly one signed admin_audit row itself (action auth.breakglass, auth_method breakglass, outcome ok|denied, client_ip). actor_sub is `breakglass:<configured username>` on a username match and `breakglass:unknown` otherwise; the submitted username and password are never stored or logged. When admin audit is enabled and the row cannot be written the login fails closed (503 audit_unavailable, no session). Rate-limited requests are aggregated into at most one audit row per IP per window. The handler always logs one ERROR line msg=breakglass_login (outcome, client_ip), independent of the alert pipeline. It also publishes an integration.Finding with RuleID `breakglass_login` through `Server.publishFinding`, a seam this ticket owns and the backup health ticket reuses: critical with DedupKey `breakglass_login:success:<session id prefix>` on success (one alert per login), high with DedupKey `breakglass_login:failure` on failure (aggregated by Count). Because Bus.PublishFinding drops findings when no alert manager exists, publishFinding falls back to an ERROR log, and the CP logs a startup WARN (W-P1-OPS1-09) when break-glass is enabled and there is no alert pipeline, or no integration's alerts.match routes rule breakglass_login.
- CP instance lock (W-P1-OPS1-05): when --state-dir is set the CP takes a non-blocking flock on `<state-dir>/warden-cp.lock` (cpstate.AcquireDirLock) for its lifetime and refuses to start if another process holds it. This also stops two CPs sharing one state dir, and it is the lock the offline backup command (W-P1-OPS1-11) and restore (W-P1-OPS1-04) check. The lock needs a local filesystem; non-unix builds refuse --state-dir.
- Backups: flags `--backup-dir` (empty means off; must not equal or sit inside --state-dir), `--backup-interval` (default 24h, min 1h), `--backup-keep` (default 7, min 1) and `--backup-include` (default `cp,alerts,config`; `fleet` is opt-in and skipped for --analytics-provider=memory). warden-fleet.db and warden-alerts.db are opened with SetMaxOpenConns(1) and no WAL, so a second connection running VACUUM INTO would make ingest and alert writes fail with SQLITE_BUSY. Each DB is therefore copied by its owning store through a new `BackupTo(ctx, path)` method that runs VACUUM INTO on that store's own *sql.DB: cpstate, integration.Store and analytics.FleetSQLiteStore (W-P1-OPS1-02). The runner, flags, manifest, schedule and pruning are W-P1-OPS1-06. Paths come from the resolved --analytics-db and --alerts-db values. The served config.yaml is copied as a file because it drives the /policy ETag today and holds the console, integrations and detection blocks.
- Set layout: a free-space check (at least 1.2x the source sizes) runs first. Files go to `<backup-dir>/.tmp-<ts>/` with dir mode 0700 and file mode 0600. manifest.json is written last (format, warden version, cpstate schema_version, ed25519 fingerprint of the admin audit public key, created_at and finished_at in UTC, files [{name, sha256, size}], skipped [...], not_included [cp-audit.key, Dex storage, secret backend]). The dir is fsynced and renamed to `<UTC ts>Z/`. Each DB copy is internally consistent; the set is not one snapshot across DBs, which is acceptable because they share no foreign keys. The sha256 manifest checks integrity, not authenticity.
- Scheduling and pruning (W-P1-OPS1-06): the next run is the newest complete set's timestamp plus the interval, so a CP that restarts nightly still backs up, and an overdue backup runs at startup. Runs never overlap. Pruning keeps the newest --backup-keep complete sets, never deletes the last good set, and removes .tmp dirs older than 24h. On-demand runs (W-P1-OPS1-11) use `warden control-plane backup` (only when no CP holds the lock) or an admin `POST /dashboard/api/backup`, which is audited, is an entry in the SSO-05 route table and, being a dashboard write, also sits behind the CP's fail-closed dashboard write guard.
- Backup health (W-P1-OPS1-07): each run logs msg=cp_backup with db, bytes, duration_ms and outcome. A failure logs ERROR and raises a `backup_failed` Finding (high, DedupKey `backup_failed:<db>`) through Server.publishFinding (W-P1-OPS1-08). A last success older than 2x the interval raises `backup_stale` (high). Last success time, last error, last set and size appear in /dashboard/api/setup for admins only. The CP has no /metrics endpoint today; CP Prometheus metrics stay with W-P5-RETN-06.
- Restore (W-P1-OPS1-04): `warden control-plane restore --from <set> --state-dir <dir> [--analytics-db] [--alerts-db] [--force] [--new-audit-key]`. It takes the CP lock and exits with 'control plane is running' if held. Before touching the target it verifies every manifest sha256 and size, runs PRAGMA integrity_check on staged copies, refuses when the set's schema_version is newer than the binary's highest migration, and refuses unless the target's cp-audit.key public key fingerprint matches the manifest (--new-audit-key overrides this and the override is recorded). A non-empty target needs --force. Existing DB, -wal and -shm files move to `<state-dir>/pre-restore-<ts>/`, staged files are renamed into place with mode 0600, and the sessions and oidc_pending tables are emptied. One admin_audit row (auth_method cli, action cp.restore, target = sha256 of manifest.json) is appended. Restore prints the backup timestamp and a warning that worker-token revocations, user blocks and policy versions made after that time must be re-applied from the shipped admin_audit JSON log, because an old snapshot can bring back revoked access.
- Docs (W-P1-OPS1-03): docs/runbooks/break-glass.md, docs/runbooks/backup-restore.md and docs/production-readiness.md (a checklist where every row names an exact flag or key). A Go test checks every command, flag and key in them against the real command tree and config.
- Tickets: W-P1-OPS1-01 hash helpers, hash-password and config; W-P1-OPS1-08 login route, limiter, session, audit and Finding (owns Server.publishFinding); W-P1-OPS1-09 startup guards, banner and degraded-mode test; W-P1-OPS1-10 L2 Dex-down test; W-P1-OPS1-02 BackupTo on the three stores; W-P1-OPS1-05 state-dir lock; W-P1-OPS1-06 backup runner; W-P1-OPS1-07 backup health Findings and setup status; W-P1-OPS1-11 admin backup trigger and offline command; W-P1-OPS1-04 restore; W-P1-OPS1-03 docs.

## Done when

Break-glass, on the compose recipe: with Dex stopped, the CP is restarted and still starts and serves /policy to workers. An operator who enabled break-glass over TLS logs in at /auth/breakglass, gets an admin session marked auth_method=breakglass with a red banner, and the session expires after 1h. The login produces exactly one signed admin_audit row, one ERROR log line and one critical breakglass_login alert that reaches a configured sink. The sixth bad attempt from one IP within 15 min gets 429. Backup and restore: a scheduled backup set taken while ingest and policy writes are in flight passes integrity_check without blocking writers. `warden control-plane restore` loads it into a fresh state dir, and is refused while a CP holds the lock and for a tampered file. The restored CP serves the same /policy ETag, worker tokens valid at backup time authenticate, earlier console sessions are invalid, and the admin audit chain verifies and ends in a cp.restore entry. A failed or stale backup raises a Finding. The Dex-stopped scenario is proved in-process by TestControlPlaneBreakGlassDegraded and against real Dex by TestBreakGlassDexDown (L2).

### 1/11 · W-P1-OPS1-01

**Add argon2id password-hash helpers, the hash-password command and console.breakGlass config validation**

Type **feature** · Size **S** · Issue [#56](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/56)

**Context.** Break-glass is an emergency local admin login for the control plane (CP) when the OIDC provider (Dex) is down. It is off by default and is delivered as four tickets: this one (W-P1-OPS1-01, GitHub #56, the foundation), W-P1-OPS1-08 (the `POST /auth/breakglass` route, rate limits, session, signed audit row and Finding; it also owns `Server.publishFinding`), W-P1-OPS1-09 (startup guards, session banner, 5-minute WARN and the degraded-mode test) and W-P1-OPS1-10 (L2 test with Dex stopped). W-P1-OPS1-01 was split from the original single break-glass ticket #56 because that ticket held a config block, a crypto helper, a CLI, an HTTP handler, a rate limiter, a session change, an audit/alert integration and startup guards across five packages.

This ticket delivers only the parts that need no HTTP handler and no session: the CP-local `console.breakGlass` config block with validation, the argon2id PHC helpers (hash, parse with bounds, verify, a fixed dummy hash), a loader for the configured hash, and the `warden control-plane hash-password` command. Nothing is mounted and nothing changes at runtime, so it merges with no behaviour change.

OUT of scope: the login route, limiter, session and audit/alert wiring (W-P1-OPS1-08); the TLS/loopback and `--state-dir` startup refusals, the red banner and the degraded-mode test (W-P1-OPS1-09).

**What to build.** The config block, `internal/controlplane/breakglass_hash.go` (new), the `hash-password` command (new `cmd/proxy/hashpassword.go`), and the two new Go dependencies with their architecture manifest entries.

**Requirements**

- Config (existing ConsoleConfig file from W-P1-SSO-02, `internal/config/console.go`): add `BreakGlass struct{Enabled bool; Username string; PasswordHashEnv string; PasswordHashFile string; SessionTTL time.Duration; AllowBehindTLSTerminator bool}` under `console.breakGlass` (yaml keys `enabled, username, passwordHashEnv, passwordHashFile, sessionTTL, allowBehindTLSTerminator`). Parsing stays strict (unknown keys fail). The block is CP-local: it never appears in `policyWire`, `SettingsWire` or the served policy JSON. Absent block = disabled, and `console.breakGlass` set on a worker config is ignored like the rest of `console:`.
- Validation when `enabled: true` (errors are `console.breakGlass.<field>: <reason>` and never contain a hash or password): `console.auth` must be `oidc`; `username` non-empty after trimming and at most 128 bytes; exactly one of `passwordHashEnv` and `passwordHashFile` is set; `sessionTTL` defaults to 1h and must be in (0, 4h]. When `enabled: false` the other fields are still parsed but not required. The check that `--state-dir` is set and that the hash parses is a startup check in W-P1-OPS1-09, not a config check, because config validation does not know the flags and must not read secrets.
- New `internal/controlplane/breakglass_hash.go`: `HashPassword(password string, random io.Reader) (string, error)` returns a PHC string `$argon2id$v=19$m=65536,t=3,p=2$<salt>$<key>` (RawStdEncoding base64; salt 16 bytes, key 32 bytes). `ParsePHC(s string) (PHC, error)` accepts only argon2id with `v=19`, m in 19456..262144 KiB, t in 2..10, p in 1..4, salt >= 16 bytes, key >= 32 bytes, total length <= 512 bytes; every error is a fixed bounded message (for example `phc: memory out of range`) that never echoes the input. `(PHC).Verify(password string) bool` runs `argon2.IDKey` and compares with `subtle.ConstantTimeCompare`. `DummyPHC() PHC` returns a fixed valid hash (default parameters) so W-P1-OPS1-08 can spend the same time on a username mismatch.
- Password rules for hashing: at least 16 runes and at most 1024 bytes; `HashPassword` returns `ErrPasswordTooShort` / `ErrPasswordTooLong`.
- `LoadBreakGlassHash(cfg config.BreakGlass) (PHC, error)`: reads the env var named by `passwordHashEnv` or the file named by `passwordHashFile` (read on every call so a mounted secret can rotate without a CP restart), trims trailing whitespace, parses it. Errors name the config key (`console.breakGlass.passwordHashEnv is empty`, `console.breakGlass.passwordHashFile: unreadable`) and never the value.
- New `cmd/proxy/hashpassword.go`: `newHashPasswordCmd()` registered as a subcommand of `warden control-plane`. There is no password flag. Without `--stdin` it reads the password from the terminal with echo off (`golang.org/x/term`), asks twice and fails with `passwords do not match` on a difference; when stdin is not a terminal and `--stdin` is not set it fails with `stdin is not a terminal; use --stdin`. With `--stdin` it reads exactly one line (trailing CR/LF removed, at most 1 KiB). It rejects passwords under 16 characters with a non-zero exit and prints nothing to stdout; on success it prints only the PHC string and a newline to stdout (prompts go to stderr). The password is never in argv, logs or error text.
- Dependencies: add `golang.org/x/crypto` (only `argon2` is imported) and `golang.org/x/term` to `go.mod` as pinned direct modules, plus any new indirect module, and add each to the S3 module manifest in `architecture.yaml` (`golang.org/x/crypto` and `golang.org/x/term` with layers `[assembly]`, indirect ones in the indirect list). `govulncheck` stays clean.
- Add a commented `console.breakGlass` example (disabled, hash from an env var, placeholder values only) to `configs/config.control-plane.yaml`.
- Back-compat: no route, no startup check and no log line changes; a config without `breakGlass` loads byte-identically.

**Implementation plan**

1. Write the failing tests first: `internal/config/console_test.go` (`TestConsoleBreakGlassValidation`), `internal/controlplane/breakglass_hash_test.go`, `cmd/proxy/hashpassword_test.go`.
2. internal/config/console.go: add the `BreakGlass` struct, strict parsing and validation; add the commented example to configs/config.control-plane.yaml.
3. Add `golang.org/x/crypto` and `golang.org/x/term` with `go get` + `go mod tidy`; add the manifest entries to architecture.yaml; run `go run ./cmd/archgen`.
4. New internal/controlplane/breakglass_hash.go: HashPassword, ParsePHC, Verify, DummyPHC, LoadBreakGlassHash.
5. New cmd/proxy/hashpassword.go: newHashPasswordCmd; register it in newControlPlaneCmd (cmd/proxy/controlplane.go).
6. Run the new tests, then `go test -race ./internal/config ./internal/controlplane ./cmd/proxy`, then scripts/check.sh.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] A table of configs (enabled with `console.auth: none`, both hash sources, neither hash source, `sessionTTL: 5h`, empty username, username of 129 bytes, and a valid block) gives the matching error naming `console.breakGlass.<field>` for each invalid one, no error for the valid one, and no error text contains a hash: `go test ./internal/config -run TestConsoleBreakGlassValidation`. Red first: the test fails before the struct exists.
- [ ] `HashPassword` output parses with `ParsePHC`, verifies the right password and rejects a wrong one; PHC strings with m=19455, m=262145, t=1, t=11, p=0, p=5, a 15-byte salt, a 31-byte key, `v=18`, `$argon2i$` and a 513-byte string are each rejected with a bounded error that does not contain the input: `go test ./internal/controlplane -run 'TestPHC'`.
- [ ] `LoadBreakGlassHash` returns the parsed hash from an env var, returns an error naming `console.breakGlass.passwordHashEnv` when it is unset, and re-reads a file after it is rewritten: `go test ./internal/controlplane -run TestLoadBreakGlassHash`.
- [ ] `warden control-plane hash-password --stdin` with a 16-character password on stdin prints exactly one line that `ParsePHC` accepts and that verifies the password; with a 15-character password it exits non-zero with empty stdout; `--password` is an unknown flag; with stdin not a terminal and no `--stdin` it fails with `stdin is not a terminal; use --stdin`; the password never appears in stdout, stderr or the error: `go test ./cmd/proxy -run TestHashPasswordCmd`.
- [ ] `go run ./cmd/archgen` leaves no diff and `go test ./internal/archtest` passes with the two new modules in the manifest; `govulncheck ./...` (run by scripts/check.sh) is clean.
- [ ] A config without a `breakGlass` block loads to the same value as before: existing `go test ./internal/config ./cmd/proxy` pass unchanged. `scripts/check.sh` passes.

**Depends on:** [`W-P1-SSO-02`](console-sso-rbac.md#211--w-p1-sso-02) Parse and validate the CP-local console config block

### 2/11 · W-P1-OPS1-02

**Add BackupTo (VACUUM INTO) to the cpstate, alert and fleet SQLite stores**

Type **feature** · Size **S** · Issue [#57](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/57)

**Context.** The CP can take scheduled backups of its SQLite state and `restore` them. That feature is delivered as: this ticket (W-P1-OPS1-02, GitHub #57, the foundation), W-P1-OPS1-05 (the CP state-dir flock), W-P1-OPS1-06 (the backup runner: flags, set layout, manifest, schedule, pruning), W-P1-OPS1-07 (backup health Findings and `/dashboard/api/setup` status), W-P1-OPS1-11 (admin `POST /dashboard/api/backup` and the `control-plane backup` command) and W-P1-OPS1-04 (verified restore, GitHub #243). W-P1-OPS1-02 was split from the original backup ticket #57, which mixed three store methods, a runner with scheduling, health reporting, an HTTP route and a CLI.

This ticket adds one consistent-copy method to each of the three stores that make up a CP backup. The fleet store (`internal/analytics/fleet_sqlite.go`) and the alert store (`internal/integration/store.go`) open their database with `SetMaxOpenConns(1)` and no WAL, so a second connection running `VACUUM INTO` would make ingest and alert writes fail with SQLITE_BUSY. Each store therefore copies itself on its own `*sql.DB`; concurrent writers queue behind the single connection instead of failing. Nothing calls the methods yet, so there is no behaviour change.

OUT of scope: choosing paths, manifests, scheduling and pruning (W-P1-OPS1-06); Findings and setup status (W-P1-OPS1-07); the trigger route and the CLI (W-P1-OPS1-11); the lock (W-P1-OPS1-05).

**What to build.** `BackupTo(ctx context.Context, dst string) error` on the cpstate DB type (package `internal/cpstate`, from W-P1-SSO-01), on `integration.Store` and on `analytics.FleetSQLiteStore`, with unit tests.

**Requirements**

- Signature on all three types: `BackupTo(ctx context.Context, dst string) error`. It runs `VACUUM INTO ?` with `dst` bound as a parameter on the store's own `*sql.DB` using `ExecContext(ctx, ...)`, so a cancelled context aborts the copy.
- `dst` must be a non-empty path whose parent directory exists and that does not exist yet; an existing `dst` is refused with a wrapped error (`backup destination exists`) before any SQL runs. On any failure the partial `dst` is removed. On success `dst` is chmod 0600.
- Writers that run while a copy is in progress wait on the store's single connection and then succeed; no caller sees SQLITE_BUSY. The method holds the connection only for the duration of the `VACUUM INTO`.
- The copy is internally consistent (one transaction) and passes `PRAGMA integrity_check`. Row contents never appear in errors or logs.
- No exported interface is added here; the runner (W-P1-OPS1-06) declares the small consumer-side interface it needs.
- `BackupTo` on the cpstate type copies the whole `warden-cp.db` including every table registered by other features (sessions, oidc_pending, admin_audit, policy versions, worker tokens); it must not filter tables.

**Implementation plan**

1. Write failing tests first in internal/cpstate, internal/integration and internal/analytics (`TestBackupTo_*`).
2. internal/cpstate (the DB type from W-P1-SSO-01): add BackupTo.
3. internal/integration/store.go: add Store.BackupTo.
4. internal/analytics/fleet_sqlite.go: add FleetSQLiteStore.BackupTo.
5. Run `go test -race ./internal/cpstate ./internal/integration ./internal/analytics -run TestBackupTo`, then scripts/check.sh.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] For each of the three stores, with 8 goroutines inserting while `BackupTo` runs, every insert succeeds without SQLITE_BUSY, the copy opens, passes `PRAGMA integrity_check` and contains every row committed before the call returned: `go test -race ./internal/cpstate ./internal/integration ./internal/analytics -run TestBackupTo_ConsistentUnderWrites`. Red first: the tests do not compile before the method exists.
- [ ] An existing `dst` is refused and left untouched; a missing parent directory returns an error and leaves no file: `go test ./internal/cpstate ./internal/integration ./internal/analytics -run TestBackupTo_Destination`.
- [ ] A context cancelled before the call returns `context.Canceled` and leaves no `dst`; a successful copy has mode 0600: `go test ./internal/cpstate ./internal/integration ./internal/analytics -run 'TestBackupTo_(Cancel|Mode)'`.
- [ ] Existing tests of the three packages pass unchanged. `scripts/check.sh` passes.

**Depends on:** [`W-P1-SSO-01`](console-sso-rbac.md#111--w-p1-sso-01) Add internal/cpstate SQLite state store with migrations

**Unblocks:** [`W-P1-OPS1-06`](ops-hardening.md#411--w-p1-ops1-06) Add the backup runner: flags, set layout, manifest, schedule and pruning

### 3/11 · W-P1-OPS1-05

**Add the CP state-dir instance lock**

Type **feature** · Size **S** · Issue —

**Context.** SQLite holds no lock that an idle CP keeps, so a flock file is the only reliable way to refuse a restore or an offline backup while a CP is running, and it also stops two CPs from sharing one state dir. This ticket (W-P1-OPS1-05) was carved out of the original restore ticket #243 (now W-P1-OPS1-04) so that the backup CLI (W-P1-OPS1-11) and restore (W-P1-OPS1-04) both depend on it and the earlier soft cycle between the backup and restore tickets disappears. P2 tickets (W-P2-KEYS-05, W-P2-KEYS-06) reuse `AcquireDirLock` for their offline commands.

OUT of scope: the restore command (W-P1-OPS1-04), the backup CLI (W-P1-OPS1-11). Token, hash-password and policy CLIs do not take the lock.

**What to build.** `cpstate.AcquireDirLock` for unix and a non-unix stub in `internal/cpstate`, and its use in `runControlPlane`.

**Requirements**

- New `internal/cpstate/lock_unix.go` (`//go:build unix`): `AcquireDirLock(dir string) (release func() error, err error)` creates or opens `<dir>/warden-cp.lock` (mode 0600, no truncate), takes `syscall.Flock(fd, LOCK_EX|LOCK_NB)`, and returns `ErrLocked` (a sentinel wrapped with the lock path, message `cpstate: state dir <dir> is locked by another process`) when the lock is held. After acquiring it writes the PID into the file for operators (informational only). `release` closes the descriptor (which drops the flock); it never deletes the file, so there is no unlink race.
- New `internal/cpstate/lock_other.go` (`//go:build !unix`): `AcquireDirLock` returns an error naming the unsupported OS, so a CP with `--state-dir` refuses to start there instead of running unlocked.
- `runControlPlane` (cmd/proxy/controlplane.go and internal/controlplane/run.go as the code is arranged) acquires the lock when `--state-dir` is set, before it opens any database or seeds the served config, and fails startup with `control plane: state dir <dir> is in use by another control plane (lock <dir>/warden-cp.lock)`. It releases the lock after the servers and stores have closed. Without `--state-dir` no lock is taken and behaviour is unchanged.
- The directory must already exist or be created by the existing state-dir setup before locking; the lock file is created inside it with 0600.
- No other command takes the lock in this ticket.

**Implementation plan**

1. Write the failing tests first: internal/cpstate/lock_test.go and a cmd/proxy test.
2. New internal/cpstate/lock_unix.go and lock_other.go.
3. Call AcquireDirLock early in runControlPlane when --state-dir is set; release on shutdown.
4. Run `go test -race ./internal/cpstate ./cmd/proxy ./internal/controlplane`, then scripts/check.sh.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] A second `AcquireDirLock` on the same dir (a second open file description, same process) returns `ErrLocked`; after `release` it succeeds: `go test ./internal/cpstate -run TestAcquireDirLock_Exclusive`. Red first: fails to compile before the function exists.
- [ ] A helper subprocess (the test binary re-executed) holds the lock and is killed with SIGKILL; the parent can then acquire it, so a crashed CP never leaves a stale lock: `go test ./internal/cpstate -run TestAcquireDirLock_ReleasedOnProcessDeath`.
- [ ] Starting a second control plane on the same `--state-dir` fails with a message containing `in use by another control plane`, the first keeps serving, and a CP without `--state-dir` starts twice without error: `go test ./cmd/proxy -run TestControlPlaneStateDirLock`.
- [ ] The lock file has mode 0600 and the lock is released on CP shutdown (a third start succeeds after the first exits): same test. `scripts/check.sh` passes.

**Depends on:** [`W-P1-SSO-01`](console-sso-rbac.md#111--w-p1-sso-01) Add internal/cpstate SQLite state store with migrations

**Unblocks:** [`W-P1-OPS1-11`](ops-hardening.md#611--w-p1-ops1-11) Add the admin backup trigger and the offline control-plane backup command; [`W-P1-OPS1-04`](ops-hardening.md#711--w-p1-ops1-04) Add the verified restore command; [`W-P1-OPS1-03`](ops-hardening.md#1111--w-p1-ops1-03) Write break-glass and backup runbooks and a production readiness guide; [`W-P2-KEYS-05`](key-management.md#57--w-p2-keys-05) Add the keys CLI, backup integration and key rotation runbook; [`W-P2-KEYS-06`](key-management.md#67--w-p2-keys-06) Add offline admin audit key rotation with a signed rotation entry

### 4/11 · W-P1-OPS1-06

**Add the backup runner: flags, set layout, manifest, schedule and pruning**

Type **feature** · Size **M** · Issue —

**Context.** The CP can write consistent, atomic, pruned backup sets of its SQLite state and served config. This ticket (W-P1-OPS1-06) was split from the original backup ticket #57 (the foundation, `BackupTo` on the stores, kept the original key W-P1-OPS1-02). It builds the runner on top of `BackupTo`. Sibling tickets: W-P1-OPS1-05 (lock), W-P1-OPS1-07 (health Findings and setup status) and W-P1-OPS1-11 (admin route and the offline CLI; uses the `BackupReporter` seam and `RunOnce` defined here), W-P1-OPS1-04 (restore; reads the manifest defined here), W-P1-OPS1-03 (docs).

OUT of scope: Findings and the `/dashboard/api/setup` fields (W-P1-OPS1-07); `POST /dashboard/api/backup` and the `control-plane backup` command (W-P1-OPS1-11); restore (W-P1-OPS1-04); CP Prometheus metrics (W-P5-RETN-06).

**What to build.** The four `--backup-*` flags, `internal/controlplane/backup.go` (new) and its tests.

**Requirements**

- Flags on `warden control-plane`: `--backup-dir` (empty means off), `--backup-interval` (default 24h, minimum 1h), `--backup-keep` (default 7, minimum 1), `--backup-include` (comma list from `cp,alerts,config,fleet`; default `cp,alerts,config`; `fleet` is opt-in). Startup validation (errors name the flag): `--backup-dir` requires `--state-dir`; it must not equal or sit inside `--state-dir` (compared after `filepath.Clean` and symlink resolution of the existing prefix); the interval, keep and include values must be valid. With `--backup-dir` unset behaviour is unchanged.
- `BackupConfig{Dir string; Interval time.Duration; Keep int; Include []string}` built in cmd/proxy/controlplane.go from the resolved state dir, `--alerts-db`, `--analytics-db` and the served config path, and passed to the CP (`controlplane.Config`).
- New `internal/controlplane/backup.go`: `BackupRunner` with `Start(ctx)`, `RunOnce(ctx) (BackupResult, error)` and `Status() BackupStatus{LastSuccessAt time.Time; LastError string; LastSet string; SizeBytes int64}`. It depends on a consumer-side interface `backupSource{BackupTo(ctx, dst string) error}` implemented by the three stores from W-P1-OPS1-02, an injectable clock and an injectable free-space function. `BackupRunner` takes an optional `BackupReporter` (`BackupFailed(db string, err error)`, `BackupSucceeded(set string)`), nil-safe, which W-P1-OPS1-07 implements.
- Sources and skips: warden-cp.db (`cp`), warden-alerts.db (`alerts`) and warden-fleet.db (`fleet`) are copied by their owning store's `BackupTo`; `config.yaml` is read once, hashed and written from the same bytes. A store that is absent (no alert store, `--analytics-provider=memory`) is not copied and is listed in the manifest `skipped` with a reason. Paths come from the resolved `--alerts-db` and `--analytics-db`.
- Before each set a free-space check requires at least 1.2x the source sizes on the backup filesystem (`syscall.Statfs` behind a `//go:build unix` file with a no-op non-unix twin); on failure the run fails with `insufficient free space` and creates nothing.
- Set layout: files are written to `<backup-dir>/.tmp-<ts>/` (dir 0700, files 0600), one DB at a time; `manifest.json` is written last with `format` (`warden.cp.backup.v1`), warden version, cpstate `schema_version` (add `SchemaVersion(ctx) (int, error)` to the cpstate DB type if W-P1-SSO-01 does not already expose one: `grep -n SchemaVersion internal/cpstate`), `audit_key_fingerprint` (the admin audit key id from W-P1-AAUD-01; omitted when `console.adminAudit.enabled` is false), `created_at` and `finished_at` in UTC, `files` [{name, sha256, size}], `skipped` [{name, reason}] and `not_included` (`cp-audit.key`, `Dex storage`, `secret backend`). Then the dir is fsynced and renamed to `<UTC ts>Z/` (`20060102T150405Z`). A set dir exists only when complete, so "complete" means has `manifest.json`. Each DB copy is internally consistent; the set is not one snapshot across DBs (they share no foreign keys). The sha256 manifest checks integrity, not authenticity (documented).
- Scheduling: one background goroutine bound to the CP context. The next run is the newest complete set's timestamp plus the interval, so a CP that restarts nightly still backs up, and an overdue backup (or no set) runs at startup without delaying CP start. Runs never overlap (a second `RunOnce` while one runs returns `ErrBackupInProgress`). Never on a request path.
- Pruning after a successful run: keep the newest `--backup-keep` complete sets, never delete the newest complete set, remove `.tmp-*` dirs older than 24h, and never touch any entry whose name is not a set name or a `.tmp-` name.
- Logging: each DB copy logs `msg=cp_backup` with `db`, `bytes`, `duration_ms`, `outcome`; failures log ERROR. No row contents are logged. A failed run reports through `BackupReporter.BackupFailed` and records `LastError` (bounded to 200 characters).

**Implementation plan**

1. Write the failing tests first (internal/controlplane/backup_test.go, cmd/proxy tests).
2. cmd/proxy/controlplane.go: add the four flags, validation and BackupConfig construction; start the runner from the CP after the stores open (internal/controlplane/run.go).
3. New internal/controlplane/backup.go: BackupRunner, set writer, manifest, free-space check, schedule, pruning; add SchemaVersion to cpstate if missing.
4. Run `go test -race ./internal/controlplane ./cmd/proxy`, then scripts/check.sh.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] With a cpstate DB, an alert store and a fleet store under writes from 8 goroutines, a backup runs, every writer succeeds without SQLITE_BUSY, each copy passes `PRAGMA integrity_check`, and the manifest sha256 and size match the files: `go test -race ./internal/controlplane -run TestBackup_ConsistentUnderWrites`. Red first: fails before the runner exists.
- [ ] With `--backup-keep=3`, 5 complete sets and one `.tmp-` dir older than 24h, pruning leaves exactly the 3 newest sets and removes the `.tmp-` dir; an unrelated file in the backup dir is untouched; the newest set is never deleted: `go test ./internal/controlplane -run TestBackup_Prune`.
- [ ] With the newest set 25h old and a 24h interval (fake clock), starting the runner triggers a backup immediately; with a fresh set the next run is scheduled at set time plus interval; with `--analytics-provider=memory` the fleet DB is listed under `skipped`: `go test ./internal/controlplane -run TestBackup_Schedule`.
- [ ] A second `RunOnce` during a run returns `ErrBackupInProgress`: `go test -race ./internal/controlplane -run TestBackup_NoOverlap`.
- [ ] With the free-space function reporting too little, the run fails with `insufficient free space` and the backup dir contains no set and no `.tmp-` dir: `go test ./internal/controlplane -run TestBackup_FreeSpaceRefused`.
- [ ] A complete set has dir mode 0700 and file mode 0600, a manifest with every field listed above, and no set dir is ever visible before `manifest.json` exists (a failure injected before the rename leaves only `.tmp-`): `go test ./internal/controlplane -run 'TestBackup_(Modes|Manifest|Atomic)'`.
- [ ] A failing run calls `BackupReporter.BackupFailed` once and records `LastError`, and the CP keeps serving /policy: `go test ./internal/controlplane -run TestBackup_ReporterCalledOnFailure`.
- [ ] `--backup-dir` inside `--state-dir`, `--backup-dir` without `--state-dir`, `--backup-interval=30m`, `--backup-keep=0` and `--backup-include=bogus` are each rejected at startup with an error naming the flag, and with no `--backup-dir` the CP starts as before: `go test ./cmd/proxy -run TestControlPlaneBackupFlags`. `scripts/check.sh` passes.

**Depends on:** [`W-P1-OPS1-02`](ops-hardening.md#211--w-p1-ops1-02) Add BackupTo (VACUUM INTO) to the cpstate, alert and fleet SQLite stores; [`W-P1-SSO-01`](console-sso-rbac.md#111--w-p1-sso-01) Add internal/cpstate SQLite state store with migrations; [`W-P1-AAUD-01`](admin-audit-log.md#18--w-p1-aaud-01) Add signed, hash-chained admin audit store on cpstate

### 5/11 · W-P1-OPS1-07

**Raise backup health Findings and expose backup status in /dashboard/api/setup**

Type **feature** · Size **S** · Issue —

**Context.** Backups that fail silently are worse than none. This ticket (W-P1-OPS1-07) makes the runner of W-P1-OPS1-06 visible: Findings when a backup fails or goes stale, and backup status in `/dashboard/api/setup`. It was split from the original backup ticket #57. A later split moved the admin `POST /dashboard/api/backup` trigger and the offline `warden control-plane backup` command to W-P1-OPS1-11, because they are a separate route and a separate command. It publishes Findings through `Server.publishFinding`, which W-P1-OPS1-08 (break-glass login) owns.

OUT of scope: the runner, manifest and pruning (W-P1-OPS1-06); the lock (W-P1-OPS1-05); the admin trigger route and the offline command (W-P1-OPS1-11); restore (W-P1-OPS1-04); CP Prometheus metrics (W-P5-RETN-06; the CP has no /metrics endpoint in P1).

**What to build.** `internal/controlplane/backup_health.go` (new) and a new field on `setupResponse`.

**Requirements**

- A `BackupReporter` implementation (W-P1-OPS1-06 seam) in `internal/controlplane/backup_health.go`: `BackupFailed(db, err)` logs ERROR `msg=cp_backup_failed` (db, bounded error) and calls `s.publishFinding` with RuleID `backup_failed`, SevHigh, DedupKey `backup_failed:<db>`. A staleness check (a ticker every max(1m, interval/4), injectable clock) publishes RuleID `backup_stale`, SevHigh, DedupKey `backup_stale` when the last success is older than 2x `--backup-interval` (or when backups are enabled and none has succeeded 2x interval after start). With no alert pipeline `publishFinding` falls back to its ERROR log (W-P1-OPS1-08). No row contents appear in logs or Findings.
- `/dashboard/api/setup` (`setupResponse` in `internal/dashboard/dashboard_v3.go`) gains `backup *struct{Enabled bool; LastSuccessAt, LastError, LastSet string; SizeBytes int64}` (json `backup,omitempty`). The dashboard gets a setter `SetBackupStatus(fn func(*http.Request) *BackupStatus)`; the CP closure returns nil unless the caller is an admin Principal (or `console.auth` is none), so viewers and editors never see the field.
- Back-compat: with `--backup-dir` unset no reporter or ticker is registered and `setup` has no `backup` field.

**Implementation plan**

1. Write the failing tests first (internal/controlplane/backup_health_test.go, internal/dashboard).
2. New internal/controlplane/backup_health.go: reporter, staleness ticker, status closure.
3. internal/dashboard/dashboard_v3.go: add backup to setupResponse and SetBackupStatus; wire it in internal/controlplane.
4. Run `go test -race ./internal/controlplane ./internal/dashboard`, then scripts/check.sh.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] With an unwritable backup dir a run logs ERROR, the fake publisher receives exactly one `backup_failed` Finding with DedupKey `backup_failed:<db>`, and the CP keeps serving /policy: `go test ./internal/controlplane -run TestBackup_FailureRaisesFinding`. Red first: fails before the reporter exists.
- [ ] With the last success 3h old, a 1h interval and a fake clock, one `backup_stale` Finding is published; with a success 90 minutes old none is: `go test ./internal/controlplane -run TestBackup_StaleRaisesFinding`.
- [ ] With no alert pipeline a failure still logs ERROR `cp_backup_failed` and does not panic: `go test ./internal/controlplane -run TestBackup_NoPipelineLogsError`.
- [ ] `GET /dashboard/api/setup` includes `backup` for an admin session and omits it for viewer and editor sessions: `go test ./internal/controlplane -run TestSetup_BackupStatusAdminOnly`.
- [ ] `go test ./internal/controlplane ./internal/dashboard` still passes with backups disabled and `setup` has no `backup` field: `go test ./internal/controlplane -run TestSetup_NoBackupFieldWhenDisabled`. `scripts/check.sh` passes.

### 6/11 · W-P1-OPS1-11

**Add the admin backup trigger and the offline control-plane backup command**

Type **feature** · Size **S** · Issue —

**Context.** The runner of W-P1-OPS1-06 takes scheduled backups. This ticket (W-P1-OPS1-11) lets an operator run one on demand, in two ways: an audited admin `POST /dashboard/api/backup` while the CP runs, and `warden control-plane backup` for a stopped CP. It was split from W-P1-OPS1-07 (itself split from the original backup ticket #57) because the route and the command are separate subsystems from the health Findings and setup status. Sibling tickets: W-P1-OPS1-02 (BackupTo), -05 (lock, which the offline command takes), -06 (runner and `RunOnce`), -07 (health Findings and setup status), -04 (restore), -03 (docs).

OUT of scope: the runner, manifest and pruning (W-P1-OPS1-06); the lock (W-P1-OPS1-05); Findings and setup status (W-P1-OPS1-07); restore (W-P1-OPS1-04); CP Prometheus metrics (W-P5-RETN-06). The trigger raises no Finding itself; a failed run is reported by the W-P1-OPS1-06 reporter.

**What to build.** One route in `internal/dashboard` registered from `internal/controlplane`, and `cmd/proxy/backupcmd.go` (new).

**Requirements**

- `POST /dashboard/api/backup`: admin role, `Audited: true`, action `backup.run`, target `backup` in the W-P1-SSO-05 route table (so `dashboard.Routes()` and the authz coverage test list it). 404 when backups are disabled, 405 for other methods, 409 `{"error":"backup_in_progress"}` when a run is active, otherwise 202 `{"started":true}` after starting `RunOnce` in a goroutine bound to the CP context. The body is ignored (read limit 1 KiB). The handler sets the audit target ref to `backup` through `adminaudit.Annotate`. The route is a dashboard write, so the existing write guard (`dashboard.SetWriteGuard`, CP `dashboardWriteGuard`) also applies and fails closed. Register it where W-P1-SSO-05 registers dashboard routes (archtest rule X9: routes.go).
- New `cmd/proxy/backupcmd.go`: `warden control-plane backup --state-dir <dir> --backup-dir <dir> [--backup-include] [--analytics-db] [--alerts-db]` takes `cpstate.AcquireDirLock(stateDir)`; if held it exits non-zero with `control plane is running; use POST /dashboard/api/backup or stop it`. Otherwise it opens the stores directly, runs `RunOnce` with the same validation as the CP flags, prints the set path and exits 0, or prints the error and exits 1. It never opens the admin audit store and never starts a server.
- Back-compat: with `--backup-dir` unset nothing is registered and `POST /dashboard/api/backup` returns 404.

**Implementation plan**

1. Write the failing tests first (internal/controlplane, internal/dashboard, cmd/proxy).
2. internal/dashboard: add the POST route handler and its Routes() entry (routes.go); wire it to the runner in internal/controlplane.
3. New cmd/proxy/backupcmd.go: the offline command; register under control-plane.
4. Run `go test -race ./internal/controlplane ./internal/dashboard ./cmd/proxy`, then scripts/check.sh.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] `POST /dashboard/api/backup`: viewer and editor get 403, an admin gets 202, a second call during a run gets 409, one `backup.run` admin_audit row is written per accepted call, with backups disabled it returns 404, and without the bearer write guard credentials (none mode) it fails closed: `go test ./internal/controlplane -run TestBackupRoute`.
- [ ] The W-P1-SSO-05 route coverage test still passes with the new route listed: `go test ./internal/dashboard ./internal/controlplane -run 'Routes|Authz'`.
- [ ] `warden control-plane backup` against a state dir held by a lock exits non-zero with `control plane is running`; against a stopped state dir it writes a complete set whose manifest lists the files: `go test ./cmd/proxy -run TestControlPlaneBackupCmd`. `scripts/check.sh` passes.

### 7/11 · W-P1-OPS1-04

**Add the verified restore command**

Type **feature** · Size **M** · Issue [#243](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/243)

**Context.** Backups are only useful if a restore is safe. This ticket (W-P1-OPS1-04, GitHub #243) adds `warden control-plane restore`, which loads a backup set written by the runner of W-P1-OPS1-06 into a CP state dir. It was split from the original ticket #243 "state-dir lock + verified restore": the lock became W-P1-OPS1-05 so that the backup CLI (W-P1-OPS1-11) and restore share it without the old soft cycle between the backup and restore tickets. Sibling tickets: W-P1-OPS1-02 (BackupTo), -05 (lock), -06 (runner, defines the set layout and manifest this command reads), -07 (health/setup), -11 (route/CLI), -03 (docs).

Restore checks sha256 hashes, integrity, schema version and the audit key before it touches the target, clears stale WAL files and console sessions, and records itself in the admin audit chain. Restoring an old set can bring back revoked access, so the command warns that later revocations, blocks and policy versions must be re-applied from the shipped admin_audit JSON log.

OUT of scope: taking backups (W-P1-OPS1-06/-11); the lock implementation (W-P1-OPS1-05); P2 additions to restore (`--revoke-api-keys` is W-P2-APIK-05, key material hints are W-P2-KEYS-05, rotated-audit-key history is W-P2-KEYS-06).

**What to build.** `cmd/proxy/restore.go` (new) and tests.

**Requirements**

- Command `warden control-plane restore --from <set> --state-dir <dir> [--analytics-db <path>] [--alerts-db <path>] [--admin-audit-key-file <path>] [--force] [--new-audit-key]`, registered under `control-plane` in `cmd/proxy/controlplane.go`. `--from` and `--state-dir` are required. DB targets default as the CP resolves them (`<state-dir>/warden-fleet.db`, alert DB sibling of the analytics DB) and can be overridden with the same two flags the CP has.
- Lock first: call `cpstate.AcquireDirLock(stateDir)` (W-P1-OPS1-05) before reading anything; when it is held exit non-zero with `control plane is running`. The lock is held for the whole restore.
- Manifest: read `manifest.json` written by W-P1-OPS1-06. An unknown `format` fails with `unsupported backup format`. Each manifest file name must be one of `warden-cp.db`, `warden-alerts.db`, `warden-fleet.db`, `config.yaml`; any other name, a path separator or `..` is refused (path traversal). Entries in `not_included` and `skipped` are never touched on the target.
- Checks before any write to the target. Files are copied into a staging directory created inside the target's own directory (mode 0700, name `.restore-<ts>`) while hashing: the sha256 and size of every file must equal the manifest (`manifest mismatch: <file>` otherwise); `PRAGMA integrity_check` must return `ok` on every staged DB; the set's cpstate `schema_version` must not exceed the binary's highest cpstate migration (`backup schema_version N is newer than this binary supports (M)`); when the manifest carries an audit key fingerprint the target's `cp-audit.key` (`--admin-audit-key-file`, default `<state-dir>/cp-audit.key`) must have the same fingerprint, unless `--new-audit-key` is passed (the override is recorded in the audit row). A manifest without a fingerprint skips the key check. A non-empty target (any of the target files exists) needs `--force` (`target state dir is not empty; pass --force`).
- Apply: existing DB, `-wal` and `-shm` files and `config.yaml` that will be replaced move to `<state-dir>/pre-restore-<ts>/` (mode 0700); staged files are renamed into place (same filesystem, atomic) with mode 0600. If a step fails the already-moved files are moved back and the command exits non-zero naming the pre-restore dir. Stale `-wal`/`-shm` files are never replayed onto the restored DB.
- Console sessions: after the swap, on the restored `warden-cp.db`, run `DELETE FROM sessions` and `DELETE FROM oidc_pending` for whichever of those tables exist (the tables come from W-P1-SSO-04 and -03; absence is not an error), so earlier cookies stop working.
- Audit: when the `admin_audit` table exists, append one row through the W-P1-AAUD-01 store (`adminaudit.Store.Append`, key from `--admin-audit-key-file`) with auth_method `cli`, action `cp.restore`, target = sha256 of manifest.json and details `{new_audit_key: bool, set_created_at}`, so the chain stays valid. If the append fails after the files are in place the command exits non-zero and says the restore is applied but unaudited.
- Output: print the backup `created_at`, warden version, restored file names and the pre-restore dir, and a warning that worker-token revocations, user blocks and policy versions made after the backup time must be re-applied from the admin_audit JSON log. No file contents, tokens or key material are printed.
- Fail closed: any check failure leaves the target byte-for-byte unchanged (staging is removed) and exits non-zero.

**Implementation plan**

1. Write the failing tests first in cmd/proxy/restore_test.go.
2. New cmd/proxy/restore.go: flag parsing, lock, manifest read and name allowlist.
3. restore.go: staging copy with hashing, integrity_check, schema and key-fingerprint checks, non-empty/--force check.
4. restore.go: move-aside to pre-restore-<ts>/, rename into place, rollback on failure.
5. restore.go: clear sessions and oidc_pending via cpstate, append the cp.restore audit row, print the summary and warning.
6. Register the command in cmd/proxy/controlplane.go; run `go test -race ./cmd/proxy -run TestControlPlaneRestore`, then scripts/check.sh.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] Back up with the W-P1-OPS1-06 runner (including a worker token created through the W-P1-WTOK-01 store, a policy head written through the W-P1-PVER-02 path and a console session), restore into an empty state dir and start the CP: GET /policy returns the same ETag, the worker token authenticates, the pre-backup session cookie gets 401, and `adminaudit.Verify` passes with one `cp.restore` entry at the end: `go test ./cmd/proxy -run TestControlPlaneRestore_RoundTrip`.
- [ ] With one flipped byte in a backed-up .db file, restore exits non-zero with `manifest mismatch: <file>` and the target dir is byte-for-byte unchanged and has no staging dir: `go test ./cmd/proxy -run TestControlPlaneRestore_TamperedFile`.
- [ ] While another holder has the lock (`cpstate.AcquireDirLock`), restore exits non-zero with `control plane is running` and changes nothing: `go test ./cmd/proxy -run TestControlPlaneRestore_RefusesWhileLocked`.
- [ ] A set with a newer `schema_version`, and a target whose `cp-audit.key` fingerprint differs from the manifest, are each refused without changes; `--new-audit-key` allows the second case and the audit row details record it: `go test ./cmd/proxy -run TestControlPlaneRestore_Refusals`.
- [ ] Stale `-wal` and `-shm` files in the target are moved to `pre-restore-<ts>/` and not replayed onto the restored DB: `go test ./cmd/proxy -run TestControlPlaneRestore_StaleWAL`.
- [ ] A manifest that lists `../x.db` or an unknown file name is refused before anything is written: `go test ./cmd/proxy -run TestControlPlaneRestore_ManifestNames`.
- [ ] A non-empty target without `--force` is refused; with `--force` the old files are found under `pre-restore-<ts>/`; a failing rename (injected through the file-ops seam of the command) rolls the moved files back: `go test ./cmd/proxy -run 'TestControlPlaneRestore_(NonEmptyNeedsForce|RollbackOnFailure)'`.
- [ ] Command output contains the backup timestamp and the re-apply warning and contains none of the file contents or the audit key: `go test ./cmd/proxy -run TestControlPlaneRestore_Output`. `scripts/check.sh` passes.

**Depends on:** [`W-P1-OPS1-06`](ops-hardening.md#411--w-p1-ops1-06) Add the backup runner: flags, set layout, manifest, schedule and pruning; [`W-P1-OPS1-05`](ops-hardening.md#311--w-p1-ops1-05) Add the CP state-dir instance lock; [`W-P1-AAUD-01`](admin-audit-log.md#18--w-p1-aaud-01) Add signed, hash-chained admin audit store on cpstate; [`W-P1-PVER-01`](policy-versioning.md#112--w-p1-pver-01) Add versioned policy store and serve the head version; [`W-P1-PVER-02`](policy-versioning.md#212--w-p1-pver-02) Route policy, settings and llmProviders writes through versioned publish; [`W-P1-WTOK-01`](worker-credentials.md#111--w-p1-wtok-01) Add worker token store with hashed storage, revocation and in-memory index; [`W-P1-SSO-04`](console-sso-rbac.md#411--w-p1-sso-04) Add server-side sessions, the session middleware, cookie and CSRF

### 8/11 · W-P1-OPS1-08

**Add POST /auth/breakglass with rate limits, a session, a signed audit row and a Finding**

Type **feature** · Size **M** · Issue —

**Context.** Break-glass is an emergency local admin login for when Dex is down. This ticket (W-P1-OPS1-08) is the login itself and was split from the original break-glass ticket #56 (foundation: W-P1-OPS1-01, GitHub #56; guards, banner and degraded-mode test: W-P1-OPS1-09; L2 Dex-down test: W-P1-OPS1-10). It uses the PHC helpers and hash loader of W-P1-OPS1-01. It also owns `Server.publishFinding`, the seam through which the CP publishes Findings; the backup health ticket (W-P1-OPS1-07) and P2/P3 tickets depend on it.

Every attempt is loud by design: one signed admin_audit row, one ERROR log line and one Finding, so break-glass use is never silent, even with no alert pipeline.

OUT of scope: startup refusals (TLS/loopback, `--state-dir`), the `/auth/me` assertions, red banner and 5-minute WARN (W-P1-OPS1-09); config and hash helpers (W-P1-OPS1-01).

**What to build.** `internal/controlplane/breakglass.go` and `ratelimit.go` (new), `Server.publishFinding`, a `SessionStore.Create` option, and the route-table entry.

**Requirements**

- Route: `POST /auth/breakglass` is mounted only when `console.breakGlass.enabled` and `console.auth: oidc`; otherwise it returns 404 and nothing is audited. In the W-P1-SSO-05 authz table it is a public pre-auth route, exempt from the W-P1-SSO-04 CSRF check and with `Audited: false` (the handler writes its own row; the W-P1-AAUD-02 middleware must not double-record). Register it with the other `/auth/*` routes (archtest X9).
- Request checks in this order: method (405 with `Allow: POST`); `Content-Type: application/json` (415); `Origin`, when present, must equal the console origin from `console.oidc.redirectURL` (403 `{"error":"origin"}`); body at most 4 KiB via `http.MaxBytesReader` (413); strict JSON `{"username","password"}` with unknown fields rejected (400).
- Rate limit then verify: first the failure limiter (new `internal/controlplane/ratelimit.go`: fixed 15-minute window with an injectable clock and a sweep of expired keys; 5 failures per `r.RemoteAddr` host, no `X-Forwarded-For` trust, plus a global ceiling of 20 failures per window). A limited request returns 429 `{"error":"rate_limited"}` with `Retry-After` and never runs argon2 (even with correct credentials). Then a 2-slot verify semaphore: when full, 429 `{"error":"busy"}` with `Retry-After`. Then argon2id: the hash is loaded with `LoadBreakGlassHash` on every attempt; if it cannot be loaded the response is 503 `{"error":"breakglass_unavailable"}` plus an ERROR log. Verification always runs exactly once: against the configured hash on a username match, against `DummyPHC()` on a mismatch, and the username is compared with `subtle.ConstantTimeCompare`, so a wrong username and a wrong password take the same time and return the same 401 body `{"error":"invalid_credentials"}`. Only 401 outcomes count as failures.
- Session: success deletes earlier break-glass sessions (`SessionStore.DeleteBySub("breakglass:<username>")`) and creates a session with role admin (the session carries `auth_method` `breakglass`), `sub` `breakglass:<configured username>`, an absolute expiry of `sessionTTL` (default 1h) and no idle extension, using a new create option on the W-P1-SSO-04 `SessionStore` (for example `CreateOptions{AbsoluteTTL}`; the idle timeout for these sessions equals the absolute TTL so activity never extends it). The cookie is the W-P1-SSO-04 console cookie and is always `Secure` for break-glass sessions, including when `allowBehindTLSTerminator` is set. Response: 200 `{"ok":true,"expiresAt":"<RFC3339>"}`; the client then calls `/auth/me`.
- Admin audit: exactly one row per attempt that is not rate limited, written by the handler through `adminaudit.Recorder` (W-P1-AAUD-01): action `auth.breakglass`, auth_method `breakglass`, outcome `ok` or `denied`, `client_ip` the RemoteAddr host, `actor_sub` `breakglass:<configured username>` on a username match and `breakglass:unknown` otherwise. Rate-limited requests add at most one row per IP per window (outcome `denied`, details reason `rate_limited`). The submitted username and password are never stored or logged. Fail closed: when admin audit is enabled and the row cannot be written, the login fails with 503 `{"error":"audit_unavailable"}` and no session is created. When admin audit is not enabled the login proceeds (the ERROR log and Finding still happen; W-P1-OPS1-09 warns at startup).
- Log and alert: every attempt logs one ERROR line `msg=breakglass_login` with `outcome`, `client_ip` and, on success, the first 8 hex characters of the session id hash. A new `Server.publishFinding(f integration.Finding)` (this ticket owns it; behind a small `FindingPublisher` interface for tests) publishes through the CP alert pipeline's bus when `s.pipeline` is non-nil and otherwise logs ERROR `msg=finding_not_published` with the rule id and severity. Findings: RuleID `breakglass_login`, SevCritical with DedupKey `breakglass_login:success:<first 8 hex of the session id hash>` on success (one alert per login), SevHigh with DedupKey `breakglass_login:failure` on a failure or rate-limited request (aggregated by Count). Finding fields carry only the outcome and client IP.
- Nothing about the response, logs, audit rows or Findings distinguishes an unknown username from a wrong password.
- Back-compat: with break-glass disabled the routes, startup, audit and existing compose recipes are unchanged.

**Implementation plan**

1. Write the failing tests first in internal/controlplane (breakglass_test.go, ratelimit_test.go).
2. internal/controlplane/ratelimit.go: failureLimiter with window, per-key and global ceilings, clock, sweep.
3. W-P1-SSO-04 SessionStore: add the absolute-TTL create option; internal/controlplane/seams.go or controlplane.go: add FindingPublisher and Server.publishFinding.
4. internal/controlplane/breakglass.go: handleBreakGlass (checks, limiter, semaphore, verify, session, audit row, log, Finding); register it only when enabled; add the public-route entry to the SSO-05 authz table.
5. Run `go test -race ./internal/controlplane`, then scripts/check.sh.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] With no `breakGlass` block `POST /auth/breakglass` returns 404 and writes no audit row or Finding: `go test ./internal/controlplane -run TestBreakGlass_DisabledReturns404`. Red first: fails before the route exists.
- [ ] Correct credentials over httptest TLS set the console session cookie with Secure; the session has role admin and auth_method breakglass; with a fake clock it is rejected at now+1h01m and not extended by activity; a second login revokes the first session; the fake publisher gets exactly one SevCritical Finding and admin_audit gets exactly one row with outcome ok: `go test ./internal/controlplane -run TestBreakGlass_Success`.
- [ ] After 5 failures from one RemoteAddr in 15 minutes the 6th attempt (even with correct credentials) gets 429 with `Retry-After` and argon2 is not called; a different RemoteAddr still gets 401 or 200 until the global ceiling of 20 is reached; after the window passes the limiter allows again; at most one audit row is written for the rate-limited requests of one IP in the window: `go test ./internal/controlplane -run TestBreakGlass_RateLimit`.
- [ ] A wrong username and a wrong password both return the same 401 body, both run argon2 exactly once, and captured logs, audit rows and Findings contain neither the submitted username nor the password: `go test ./internal/controlplane -run TestBreakGlass_NoEnumerationNoLeak`.
- [ ] Wrong method (405), wrong content type (415), a foreign Origin (403), a 5 KiB body (413) and unknown JSON fields (400) are rejected before argon2 runs: `go test ./internal/controlplane -run TestBreakGlass_RequestChecks`.
- [ ] With the admin audit store failing, a correct login returns 503 `audit_unavailable` and creates no session: `go test ./internal/controlplane -run TestBreakGlass_AuditFailureDeniesLogin`.
- [ ] With no alert pipeline (`s.pipeline` nil) a login still writes the audit row and exactly one ERROR line `msg=breakglass_login`, and `publishFinding` logs `finding_not_published`: `go test ./internal/controlplane -run TestBreakGlass_NoPipelineStillLoud`.
- [ ] An unreadable hash file returns 503 `breakglass_unavailable` and creates no session; a rotated hash file takes effect without restart: `go test ./internal/controlplane -run TestBreakGlass_HashReload`.
- [ ] The W-P1-SSO-05 route coverage test passes with the new public route listed. `scripts/check.sh` passes.

**Depends on:** [`W-P1-OPS1-01`](ops-hardening.md#111--w-p1-ops1-01) Add argon2id password-hash helpers, the hash-password command and console.breakGlass config validation; [`W-P1-SSO-04`](console-sso-rbac.md#411--w-p1-sso-04) Add server-side sessions, the session middleware, cookie and CSRF; [`W-P1-SSO-05`](console-sso-rbac.md#511--w-p1-sso-05) Enforce role checks on every dashboard route and replace the bearer write guard in oidc mode; [`W-P1-AAUD-01`](admin-audit-log.md#18--w-p1-aaud-01) Add signed, hash-chained admin audit store on cpstate; [`W-P1-AAUD-02`](admin-audit-log.md#28--w-p1-aaud-02) Record CP admin mutations through audit middleware

**Unblocks:** [`W-P1-BLOCK-07`](user-block-list.md#712--w-p1-block-07) Deny console login and sessions for blocked principals; [`W-P1-OPS1-07`](ops-hardening.md#511--w-p1-ops1-07) Raise backup health Findings and expose backup status in /dashboard/api/setup; [`W-P1-OPS1-09`](ops-hardening.md#911--w-p1-ops1-09) Add break-glass startup guards, the session banner and the degraded-mode test; [`W-P1-OPS1-03`](ops-hardening.md#1111--w-p1-ops1-03) Write break-glass and backup runbooks and a production readiness guide; [`W-P2-APPR-04`](policy-approvals.md#49--w-p2-appr-04) Add the change draft API with the two-person rule; [`W-P2-APPR-07`](policy-approvals.md#79--w-p2-appr-07) Add audited break-glass emergency apply with post-hoc review; [`W-P2-APIK-05`](api-keys.md#57--w-p2-apik-05) Add offline API key revoke, restore revocation and expiry warnings; [`W-P3-OFFB-01`](offboarding.md#17--w-p3-offb-01) Implement the resumable two-stage Offboarder; [`W-P3-OFFB-02`](offboarding.md#27--w-p3-offb-02) Add the IdP refresh job in observe mode with safe token write-back

### 9/11 · W-P1-OPS1-09

**Add break-glass startup guards, the session banner and the degraded-mode test**

Type **feature** · Size **S** · Issue —

**Context.** The last piece of break-glass, split from the original ticket #56 (foundation W-P1-OPS1-01, login W-P1-OPS1-08). This ticket (W-P1-OPS1-09) makes enabling break-glass safe and proves the whole point of the feature: with the OIDC issuer unreachable the CP still starts, still serves workers, and the break-glass login still works. It relies on lazy OIDC discovery from W-P1-SSO-03 (`/auth/login` answers 503 `idp_unavailable` while discovery retries).

OUT of scope: the login route and Findings (W-P1-OPS1-08); the real-Dex compose test (W-P1-OPS1-10); runbooks (W-P1-OPS1-03).

**What to build.** Startup validation in `cmd/proxy/controlplane.go`, a ticker in the CP, a banner in `internal/dashboard/index.html`, and tests.

**Requirements**

- Startup validation (new `validateBreakGlassStartup` in cmd/proxy/controlplane.go; cmd stays construction only, the logic lives in a function the test calls): when `console.breakGlass.enabled`, fail startup with a message naming the key when `--state-dir` is empty; when the hash does not load or violates the bounds (error names `console.breakGlass.passwordHashEnv` or `passwordHashFile`, never the value); and when the CP would serve plain HTTP (no `--ca-cert`/`--ca-key`) on a non-loopback `--listen` address (`0.0.0.0`, `::`, an empty host such as `:7070`, or a non-loopback IP/host) unless `allowBehindTLSTerminator` is true. Loopback means `127.0.0.0/8`, `::1` or `localhost`.
- Startup WARNs (log only): break-glass is enabled and there is no alert pipeline, or no configured integration's `alerts.match` routes a synthetic Finding with RuleID `breakglass_login` and severity critical (use the same matcher the integration router uses); break-glass is enabled while `console.adminAudit.enabled` is false.
- `/auth/me` (W-P1-SSO-04) already returns `authMethod` and `expiresAt`; this ticket adds no fields and asserts that a break-glass session reports `authMethod: "breakglass"` and `expiresAt` equal to creation plus `sessionTTL`.
- Banner: `internal/dashboard/index.html` shows a red banner (element id `breakglass-banner`, text `Break-glass session, expires at <time>`) whenever `/auth/me` reports `authMethod` `breakglass`; the time is set with `textContent` or `esc()`, never raw HTML.
- While at least one break-glass session is active the CP logs a WARN `msg=breakglass_session_active` (count, earliest expiry) every 5 minutes, driven by an injectable ticker started from `Server.Start`; it uses `SessionStore.List` and logs no session ids beyond 8 hex characters.
- Degraded mode: with `console.auth: oidc`, break-glass enabled and the OIDC issuer unreachable at CP start, the CP starts and serves `/policy`, `/control/heartbeat` and `/central/ingest`, `/auth/login` returns 503 `idp_unavailable`, and `/auth/breakglass` logs in.
- Back-compat: with break-glass disabled none of the checks, WARNs, tickers or banner logic run.

**Implementation plan**

1. Write the failing tests first (cmd/proxy/commands_test.go, internal/controlplane, internal/dashboard).
2. cmd/proxy/controlplane.go: add validateBreakGlassStartup and the two WARNs; call it before the CP starts.
3. internal/controlplane: add the 5-minute ticker in Server.Start.
4. internal/dashboard/index.html: add the banner element and the /auth/me check.
5. Add TestControlPlaneBreakGlassDegraded; run `go test -race ./cmd/proxy ./internal/controlplane ./internal/dashboard`, then scripts/check.sh.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] Enabled with `console.auth: none`, a PHC with m below 19456, an unset hash env, no `--state-dir`, or plain HTTP on `0.0.0.0:7070` / `:7070` without `allowBehindTLSTerminator` each fail with an error naming the key or flag and never containing the hash; loopback listen, `--ca-cert/--ca-key`, and `allowBehindTLSTerminator: true` each pass: `go test ./cmd/proxy -run TestControlPlaneBreakGlassStartup`. Red first: fails before the function exists.
- [ ] With no alert route for `breakglass_login`, and with admin audit disabled, the startup WARNs are logged exactly once each, and not logged when a matching route exists: `go test ./cmd/proxy -run TestControlPlaneBreakGlassWarns`.
- [ ] A break-glass session created through `SessionStore.Create` reports `authMethod: breakglass` and `expiresAt` = created + sessionTTL from `/auth/me`: `go test ./internal/controlplane -run TestBreakGlass_MeFields`.
- [ ] With a fake ticker, an active break-glass session produces a WARN `breakglass_session_active` per tick and an expired or absent one produces none: `go test ./internal/controlplane -run TestBreakGlass_SessionWarn`.
- [ ] The served index.html contains `breakglass-banner`, compares `authMethod` with `breakglass`, and sets the expiry through `textContent` or `esc(`: `go test ./internal/dashboard -run TestIndexBreakGlassBanner`.
- [ ] With the OIDC issuer unreachable, the CP starts and serves /policy, heartbeat and ingest, `/auth/login` returns 503 `idp_unavailable`, and a break-glass login yields an admin session, one admin_audit row and one ERROR line `msg=breakglass_login` even with zero integrations: `go test ./cmd/proxy -run TestControlPlaneBreakGlassDegraded`.
- [ ] With `breakGlass` absent or disabled, existing tests pass unchanged and `/auth/breakglass` is 404: `go test ./cmd/proxy ./internal/controlplane ./internal/dashboard`. `scripts/check.sh` passes.

### 10/11 · W-P1-OPS1-10

**Add the L2 break-glass test with Dex stopped**

Type **test** · Size **S** · Issue —

**Context.** The done-when of the break-glass and backup feature says: with Dex stopped, the CP is restarted and still serves workers, and an operator can log in with break-glass over TLS. The L1 test `TestControlPlaneBreakGlassDegraded` (W-P1-OPS1-09) proves it with a fake issuer; this ticket (W-P1-OPS1-10, new) proves it against the real Dex container using the L2 identity stack from W-P1-DEX-04. It exists because that scenario had no automated owner after the split of #56.

OUT of scope: the L1 test (W-P1-OPS1-09); the runbook text (W-P1-OPS1-03).

**What to build.** One L2 test in `test/e2e` (build tag `e2e`).

**Requirements**

- New `test/e2e/breakglass_test.go` (`//go:build e2e`) with `TestBreakGlassDexDown`, using the identity stack helpers of W-P1-DEX-04 (Dex, CP in oidc mode, a worker). The CP is configured with `console.breakGlass` enabled, a hash produced in the test with `controlplane.HashPassword`, TLS from the e2e certs, and the hash passed through an env var.
- Flow: stack up and the worker synced; stop the Dex container; restart the CP container; assert the worker still receives `/policy` (ETag unchanged) and heartbeats, `/auth/login` returns 503 `idp_unavailable`; log in at `/auth/breakglass` with a Go HTTP client whose dialer is overridden to reach the published CP port (no /etc/hosts edits); assert `/auth/me` shows `authMethod` `breakglass`, the CP log contains exactly one `msg=breakglass_login` ERROR line, and a bad-password attempt leaves one `denied` audit row.
- The test skips with a clear message unless the L2 environment is available, like the other tests in test/e2e. No real external account is used; the password in the test is generated per run and never logged.

**Implementation plan**

1. Read test/e2e/shared.go and the W-P1-DEX-04 helpers; write the test.
2. Run `make e2e-scenario NAME=TestBreakGlassDexDown` where Docker is available (CI job e2e).

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] `make e2e-scenario NAME=TestBreakGlassDexDown` passes in the CI `e2e` job: after Dex is stopped and the CP restarted, /policy still reaches the worker, /auth/login is 503, and the break-glass login produces an admin session, one ERROR log line and one audit row.
- [ ] `go vet -tags e2e ./test/e2e/...` is clean and `go test ./test/e2e` without the tag compiles nothing from this file. `scripts/check.sh` passes.

### 11/11 · W-P1-OPS1-03

**Write break-glass and backup runbooks and a production readiness guide**

Type **docs** · Size **S** · Issue [#58](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/58)

**Context.** This is the documentation ticket of the break-glass and backup feature (GitHub #58). It lands after the code tickets: W-P1-OPS1-01 (hash-password), W-P1-OPS1-08 and -09 (break-glass login and guards), W-P1-OPS1-05 (lock), W-P1-OPS1-06, -07 and -11 (backups) and W-P1-OPS1-04 (restore), plus the other Phase 1 settings the readiness checklist names (W-P1-SSO-06, W-P1-WTOK-04, W-P1-JAUD-03, W-P1-AAUD-03). The Dex-down drill is proven by W-P1-OPS1-10 and the restore round trip by W-P1-OPS1-04; this ticket documents the commands those tests run and keeps the docs from drifting away from the CLI.

OUT of scope: any behaviour change; new flags or keys.

**What to build.** Three documents, a commented compose change and a Go test that checks the docs against the real command tree and config.

**Requirements**

- New `docs/runbooks/backup-restore.md`: the `--backup-*` flags and defaults, set layout and manifest fields, copying complete sets off host (skip `.tmp-*` dirs), the on-demand `warden control-plane backup` and `POST /dashboard/api/backup`, the state-dir lock and that it needs a local filesystem (flock on NFS is not reliable), a restore drill (stop CP, run `warden control-plane restore`, start CP, compare the `/policy` ETag, run the admin audit verify), re-applying worker-token revocations, user blocks and policy versions made after the backup from the shipped admin_audit JSON log, and what is outside a set (`cp-audit.key`, Dex storage, the CA cert and key, secret backend contents).
- New `docs/runbooks/break-glass.md`: generate a hash with `warden control-plane hash-password --stdin`, store it in the env var or file named by `console.breakGlass` (never in config.yaml), the TLS requirement, logging in during a Dex outage with an example `curl --resolve` request and the 200/401/404/429/503 responses, the 1h session and red banner, rotating or disabling the hash afterwards, reviewing admin log entries with `auth_method` breakglass, and confirming the `breakglass_login` alert fired. It also states that rate limits are in memory and reset on CP restart.
- New `docs/production-readiness.md`: one row per item with the exact flag or key and how to check it: `--ca-cert`/`--ca-key`, `console.auth: oidc` with an https issuer, `console.adminAudit.enabled: true`, `--require-worker-tokens` with TLS and without `--allow-insecure-worker-auth`, `--backup-dir` with an off-host copy, `console.breakGlass` (disabled, or enabled with a rotated hash and an alert route for `breakglass_login` and `backup_failed`), and the JSON audit output from p1-json-audit.
- `deploy/compose/docker-compose.control-plane.yml`: add a named backup volume mounted into the CP service and the backup flags as commented lines so the drill runs as written.
- No real secrets: every example PHC string is marked as a placeholder on the same line, and every command reads secrets from env, a file or stdin.
- `docs/control-plane.md` links the three new files; the README docs index links `docs/production-readiness.md`.
- New Go test file `cmd/proxy/docs_test.go`: `lintDocCommands` extracts fenced `warden control-plane ...` and `go run ./cmd/proxy control-plane ...` lines from the three docs and checks every subcommand and `--flag` against the cobra tree built by `newControlPlaneCmd()`/`newRootCmd`; a second test resolves every dotted config key in backticks in `docs/production-readiness.md` against the yaml tags of the config structs by reflection. These replace the manual drills the earlier version of this ticket asked for.

**Implementation plan**

1. Write the failing docs tests first (cmd/proxy/docs_test.go) with the docs absent.
2. Write docs/runbooks/backup-restore.md, docs/runbooks/break-glass.md and docs/production-readiness.md; take every command from `go run ./cmd/proxy control-plane --help` and the subcommand help.
3. Update deploy/compose/docker-compose.control-plane.yml (backup volume, commented flags).
4. Link the new files from docs/control-plane.md and the README docs index.
5. Run `go run docs/roadmap/gen.go check`, the docs tests and scripts/check.sh.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] Every `warden control-plane` / `go run ./cmd/proxy control-plane` command in the three docs names an existing subcommand and existing flags; a doc line with a flag that does not exist (negative case built in the test from a string) fails the lint and names the flag: `go test ./cmd/proxy -run TestRunbookCommandsMatchCLI`.
- [ ] Every flag in `docs/production-readiness.md` exists in the control-plane or run command tree and every dotted config key resolves to a yaml field: `go test ./cmd/proxy -run TestProductionReadinessKeysExist`.
- [ ] Every line in docs/runbooks and docs/production-readiness.md that matches `--password` or `$argon2id$` also contains the word `placeholder`: `go test ./cmd/proxy -run TestRunbooksHaveNoRealSecrets`.
- [ ] `deploy/compose/docker-compose.control-plane.yml` still parses as YAML, declares a backup volume mounted in the control-plane service, and contains the commented `--backup-dir` line: `go test ./cmd/proxy -run TestComposeControlPlaneBackupVolume`.
- [ ] `docs/control-plane.md` contains links to `runbooks/backup-restore.md`, `runbooks/break-glass.md` and `production-readiness.md`: `go test ./cmd/proxy -run TestControlPlaneDocLinksRunbooks`.
- [ ] The documented restore drill is exactly the command sequence exercised by `go test ./cmd/proxy -run TestControlPlaneRestore_RoundTrip` (W-P1-OPS1-04) and the break-glass drill by `go test ./cmd/proxy -run TestControlPlaneBreakGlassDegraded` (W-P1-OPS1-09) and `make e2e-scenario NAME=TestBreakGlassDexDown` (W-P1-OPS1-10); the runbooks name those tests.
- [ ] `go run docs/roadmap/gen.go check` reports no stale generated files. `scripts/check.sh` passes.
